requirements.canonical: A deterministic external function IS safe to be called from the specific places listed in clause 16.1.4, where non-determinism could lead to unexpected side effects.
requirements.original: Deterministic functions are safe to be used when called from specific places where non-determinism could lead to unexpected side effects (see clause 16.1.4).

ambiguity.issue: The sentence speaks of 'deterministic functions' in general but appears in the external function clause; the glossary term 'deterministic function' is broader. Read as deterministic external functions.

requirements.subject: ent:control-modifier
requirements.canonical: The `@control` modifier of an external function IS used in the same way as for functions, as described in clause 16.1.5.
requirements.original: The @control modifier is used in the same way as described in clause 16.1.5.

requirements.subject: ent:external-function
requirements.canonical: An external function SHOULD exchange information with the test system only via return values and parameter passing.
requirements.original: NOTE: External functions should only exchange information with the test system via return values and parameter passing.

requirements.subject: ent:external-function
requirements.canonical: An external function SHOULD NOT cause side effects that change the status of the test system and may influence the test outcome.
requirements.original: Side-effects that change the status of the test system and may influence the test outcome should be avoided.

requirements.subject: ent:side-effect
requirements.canonical: A side effect that changes the status of the test system CAN occur if an external function contains default handling, configuration, communication or timer operations.
requirements.original: Such side-effects can occur if an external function contains default handling, configuration, communication or timer operations.

requirements.subject: ent:value-returning-function
requirements.condition: a value returning function is called in a receiving communication operation, a timeout operation, a guard or event of an alt statement or altstep, or an initialization of an altstep local definition
requirements.canonical: If a value returning function is called in a receiving communication operation (in templates, template fields, in-line templates as actual parameters or when evaluating the port expression), in a timeout operation (when evaluating the timer expression), in a guard or event of an alt statement or altstep, or in the initialization of an altstep local definition, the function SHALL NOT contain any of the operations listed in clause 16.1.4 items a) to m).
requirements.original: If value returning functions are called in receiving communication operations (in templates, template fields, in-line templates as actual parameters or when evaluating the port expression), in timeout operations (when evaluating the timer expression), in test component operations (in guards or events of alt statements or altsteps, see clause 20.2), or in initializations of altstep local definitions (see clause 16.2.1), the following operations shall not be present in functions called in the cases specified above, in order to avoid side effects that cause changing the state of the component or the actual snapshot and to prevent different results of subsequent evaluations on an unchanged snapshot:

improper_terms.used: test component operations (in guards or events of alt statements or altsteps)
improper_terms.proper: alternatives (guards and events) of alt statements or altsteps

ambiguity.issue: 'test component operations' normally denotes create/start/stop/done etc.; the parenthesis shows that guards and events of alt statements and altsteps are meant.

requirements.subject: ent:value-returning-function
requirements.canonical: The restriction on operations in functions called from snapshot-evaluation contexts IS intended to avoid side effects that change the component state or the actual snapshot and to prevent different results of subsequent evaluations on an unchanged snapshot.
requirements.original: If value returning functions are called in receiving communication operations (in templates, template fields, in-line templates as actual parameters or when evaluating the port expression), in timeout operations (when evaluating the timer expression), in test component operations (in guards or events of alt statements or altsteps, see clause 20.2), or in initializations of altstep local definitions (see clause 16.2.1), the following operations shall not be present in functions called in the cases specified above, in order to avoid side effects that cause changing the state of the component or the actual snapshot and to prevent different results of subsequent evaluations on an unchanged snapshot:

requirements.subject: ent:component-operation
requirements.condition: a value returning function is called in a receiving communication operation, a timeout operation, a guard or event of an alt statement or altstep, or an initialization of an altstep local definition
requirements.canonical: A function called (directly or indirectly) in a receiving communication operation, a timeout operation, an alt statement or altstep guard or event, or an altstep local definition initialization SHALL NOT contain a component operation (`create`, `start` (component), `stop` (component), `kill`, `running` (component), `alive`, `done` or `killed`).
requirements.original: a) All component operations, i.e. create, `start (component),` `stop (component),` `kill,` running (component), alive, done and killed (see notes 1, 3, 4 and 6).

requirements.subject: ent:port-operation
requirements.condition: a value returning function is called in a receiving communication operation, a timeout operation, a guard or event of an alt statement or altstep, or an initialization of an altstep local definition
requirements.canonical: A function called (directly or indirectly) in a receiving communication operation, a timeout operation, an alt statement or altstep guard or event, or an altstep local definition initialization SHALL NOT contain a port operation (`start` (port), `stop` (port), `halt`, `clear`, `checkstate`, `send`, `receive`, `trigger`, `call`, `getcall`, `reply`, `getreply`, `raise`, `catch`, `check`, `connect`, `disconnect`, `map` or `unmap`).
requirements.original:
b) All port operations, i.e. start (port), stop (port), halt, clear, checkstate, send, receive, trigger, call, getcall, reply, getreply, raise, catch, check, connect, disconnect,
  map and unmap (see notes 1, 2, 3, 4 and 6).

requirements.subject: ent:action-operation
requirements.condition: a value returning function is called in a receiving communication operation, a timeout operation, a guard or event of an alt statement or altstep, or an initialization of an altstep local definition
requirements.canonical: A function called (directly or indirectly) in a receiving communication operation, a timeout operation, an alt statement or altstep guard or event, or an altstep local definition initialization SHALL NOT contain the `action` operation.
requirements.original: c) The action operation (see notes 2 and 6).

requirements.subject: ent:timer-operation
requirements.condition: a value returning function is called in a receiving communication operation, a timeout operation, a guard or event of an alt statement or altstep, or an initialization of an altstep local definition
requirements.canonical: A function called (directly or indirectly) in a receiving communication operation, a timeout operation, an alt statement or altstep guard or event, or an altstep local definition initialization SHALL NOT contain a timer operation (`start` (timer), `stop` (timer), `running` (timer), `read` or `timeout`).
requirements.original: d) All timer operations, i.e. start (timer), stop (timer), running (timer), read, timeout (see notes 4 and 6).

requirements.subject: ent:non-deterministic-external-function
requirements.condition: a value returning function is called in a receiving communication operation, a timeout operation, a guard or event of an alt statement or altstep, or an initialization of an altstep local definition
requirements.canonical: A function called (directly or indirectly) in a receiving communication operation, a timeout operation, an alt statement or altstep guard or event, or an altstep local definition initialization SHALL NOT call a non-deterministic external function.
requirements.original: e) Calling non-deterministic external functions, i.e. external functions where the resulting values for actual inout or out parameters or the return value may differ for different invocations with the same actual in and inout parameters (see notes 4 and 6).

requirements.subject: ent:non-deterministic-external-function
requirements.canonical: A non-deterministic external function IS an external function whose resulting values for actual inout or out parameters or whose return value may differ for different invocations with the same actual in and inout parameters.
requirements.original: e) Calling non-deterministic external functions, i.e. external functions where the resulting values for actual inout or out parameters or the return value may differ for different invocations with the same actual in and inout parameters (see notes 4 and 6).

requirements.subject: ent:fn-rnd
requirements.condition: a value returning function is called in a receiving communication operation, a timeout operation, a guard or event of an alt statement or altstep, or an initialization of an altstep local definition
requirements.canonical: A function called (directly or indirectly) in a receiving communication operation, a timeout operation, an alt statement or altstep guard or event, or an altstep local definition initialization SHALL NOT call the `rnd` predefined function.
requirements.original: f) Calling the rnd predefined function (see notes 4 and 6).

requirements.subject: ent:component-variable
requirements.condition: a value returning function is called in a receiving communication operation, a timeout operation, a guard or event of an alt statement or altstep, or an initialization of an altstep local definition
requirements.canonical: A function called (directly or indirectly) in a receiving communication operation, a timeout operation, an alt statement or altstep guard or event, or an altstep local definition initialization SHALL NOT use a component variable on the left-hand side of an assignment.
requirements.original: g) Changing of component variables, i.e. using component variables on the left-hand side of assignments, and in the instantiation of out and inout parameters (see notes 4 and 6).

requirements.subject: ent:component-variable
requirements.condition: a value returning function is called in a receiving communication operation, a timeout operation, a guard or event of an alt statement or altstep, or an initialization of an altstep local definition
requirements.canonical: A function called (directly or indirectly) in a receiving communication operation, a timeout operation, an alt statement or altstep guard or event, or an altstep local definition initialization SHALL NOT pass a component variable as actual parameter to an `out` or `inout` formal parameter.
requirements.original: g) Changing of component variables, i.e. using component variables on the left-hand side of assignments, and in the instantiation of out and inout parameters (see notes 4 and 6).

requirements.subject: ent:setverdict-operation
requirements.condition: a value returning function is called in a receiving communication operation, a timeout operation, a guard or event of an alt statement or altstep, or an initialization of an altstep local definition
requirements.canonical: A function called (directly or indirectly) in a receiving communication operation, a timeout operation, an alt statement or altstep guard or event, or an altstep local definition initialization SHALL NOT call the `setverdict` operation.
requirements.original: h) Calling the setverdict operation (see notes 4 and 6).

requirements.subject: ent:activate-operation
requirements.condition: a value returning function is called in a receiving communication operation, a timeout operation, a guard or event of an alt statement or altstep, or an initialization of an altstep local definition
requirements.canonical: A function called (directly or indirectly) in a receiving communication operation, a timeout operation, an alt statement or altstep guard or event, or an altstep local definition initialization SHALL NOT contain the `activate` or `deactivate` statement.
requirements.original: i) Activation and deactivation of defaults, i.e. the activate and deactivate statements (see notes 5 and 6).

requirements.subject: ent:deactivate-operation
requirements.condition: a value returning function is called in a receiving communication operation, a timeout operation, a guard or event of an alt statement or altstep, or an initialization of an altstep local definition
requirements.canonical: A function called (directly or indirectly) in a receiving communication operation, a timeout operation, an alt statement or altstep guard or event, or an altstep local definition initialization SHALL NOT contain the `deactivate` statement.
requirements.original: i) Activation and deactivation of defaults, i.e. the activate and deactivate statements (see notes 5 and 6).

requirements.subject: ent:function
requirements.condition: a value returning function is called in a receiving communication operation, a timeout operation, a guard or event of an alt statement or altstep, or an initialization of an altstep local definition
requirements.canonical: A function called (directly or indirectly) in a receiving communication operation, a timeout operation, an alt statement or altstep guard or event, or an altstep local definition initialization SHALL NOT call a function or a deterministic external function with `out` or `inout` parameters.
requirements.original: j) Calling functions and deterministic external functions with out or inout parameters (see notes 7 and 8).

requirements.subject: ent:fuzzy-modifier
requirements.condition: a value returning function is called in a receiving communication operation, a timeout operation, a guard or event of an alt statement or altstep, or an initialization of an altstep local definition
requirements.canonical: A function called (directly or indirectly) in a receiving communication operation, a timeout operation, an alt statement or altstep guard or event, or an altstep local definition initialization SHALL NOT call a function or external function that has `@fuzzy` formal parameters or `@fuzzy` variables.
requirements.original: k) Calling functions and external functions with @fuzzy formal parameters and variables (see notes 4 and 9).

readings: A function called (directly or indirectly) in a receiving communication operation, a timeout operation, an alt statement or altstep guard or event, or an altstep local definition initialization SHALL NOT call a function or external function that has `@fuzzy` formal parameters or declares `@fuzzy` variables.

A function called (directly or indirectly) in a receiving communication operation, a timeout operation, an alt statement or altstep guard or event, or an altstep local definition initialization SHALL NOT call a function or external function with `@fuzzy` formal parameters, and SHALL NOT reference `@fuzzy` variables.
ambiguity.issue: The scope of 'and variables' is unclear (variables of the called function vs. variables referenced by the calling function); the first reading is used. Item m) covers referencing fuzzy variables anyway.

requirements.subject: ent:setencode-operation
requirements.condition: a value returning function is called in a receiving communication operation, a timeout operation, a guard or event of an alt statement or altstep, or an initialization of an altstep local definition
requirements.canonical: A function called (directly or indirectly) in a receiving communication operation, a timeout operation, an alt statement or altstep guard or event, or an altstep local definition initialization SHALL NOT contain the `setencode` operation.
requirements.original: l) The setencode operation (see note 8 and clause 27.9).

requirements.subject: ent:lazy-modifier
requirements.condition: a value returning function is called in a receiving communication operation, a timeout operation, a guard or event of an alt statement or altstep, or an initialization of an altstep local definition
requirements.canonical: A function called (directly or indirectly) in a receiving communication operation, a timeout operation, an alt statement or altstep guard or event, or an altstep local definition initialization SHALL NOT reference a lazy or fuzzy variable, parameter or template that has not been declared deterministic.
requirements.original: m) Referencing lazy or fuzzy variables, parameters or templates that have not been declared deterministic.

readings: A function called (directly or indirectly) in a receiving communication operation, a timeout operation, an alt statement or altstep guard or event, or an altstep local definition initialization SHALL NOT reference a `@lazy` or `@fuzzy` variable, formal parameter or template unless it is declared with the `@deterministic` modifier.

A function called (directly or indirectly) in a receiving communication operation, a timeout operation, an alt statement or altstep guard or event, or an altstep local definition initialization SHALL NOT reference a `@lazy` or `@fuzzy` object unless the referenced object's evaluation is otherwise known to be deterministic.
ambiguity.issue: 'declared deterministic' is not tied to an explicit syntax in this clause; the first reading (the @deterministic modifier on the lazy/fuzzy declaration) is used. Item m) also overlaps with item k) for fuzzy objects.

requirements.subject: ent:snapshot
requirements.canonical: The execution of the operations `start`, `stop`, `done`, `killed`, `halt`, `clear`, `receive`, `trigger`, `getcall`, `getreply`, `catch` and `check` CAN cause changes to the current snapshot.
requirements.original: NOTE 1: The execution of the operations start, stop, done, killed, halt, clear, receive, trigger, getcall, getreply, catch and check can cause changes to the current snapshot.

requirements.subject: ent:error
requirements.canonical: The use of the operations `send`, `call`, `reply`, `raise` and `action` in a function called from a snapshot-evaluation context IS an error, because all communication is to be made explicit.
requirements.original: NOTE 2: The use of operations send, call, reply, raise, and action causes an error, i.e. all communication are to be made explicit and not as a side effect of another communication operation or the evaluation of a snapshot.

requirements.subject: ent:error
requirements.canonical: The use of the operations `map`, `unmap`, `connect`, `disconnect` and `create` in a function called from a snapshot-evaluation context IS an error, because all configuration operations are to be made explicit.
requirements.original: NOTE 3: The use of operations map, unmap, connect, disconnect, create will lead to an error, i.e. all configuration operations are to be made explicit, and not as a side effect of a communication operation or the evaluation of a snapshot.

requirements.subject: ent:error
requirements.canonical: Calling non-deterministic external functions, `rnd`, `running`, `alive`, `read`, `checkstate` or `setverdict`, referencing fuzzy objects and writing to component variables in a function called from a snapshot-evaluation context IS an error, because it may lead to different results of subsequent evaluations of the same snapshot (e.g. rendering deadlock detection impossible).
requirements.original: NOTE 4: Calling of non-deterministic external functions, rnd, running, alive, read, checkstate, setverdict, referencing fuzzy objects and writing to component variables causes an error because this may lead to different results of subsequent evaluations of the same snapshot, thus, e.g. rendering deadlock detection impossible.

requirements.subject: ent:error
requirements.canonical: The use of the `activate` and `deactivate` operations in a function called from a snapshot-evaluation context IS an error, because they modify the set of defaults considered during the evaluation of the current snapshot.
requirements.original: NOTE 5: The use of operations activate and deactivate causes an error because they modify the set of defaults that is considered during the evaluation of the current snapshot.

requirements.subject: ent:value-returning-function
requirements.canonical: The restrictions of clause 16.1.4, except restriction j) on out or inout parameterization, apply recursively, i.e. the restricted operations SHALL NOT be used directly or via an arbitrarily long chain of function invocations.
requirements.original: NOTE 6: Restrictions except the limitation on the use of out or inout parameterization in restriction j) apply recursively, i.e. it is disallowed to use them directly, or via an arbitrary long chain of function invocations.

requirements.subject: ent:function
requirements.canonical: A function called from a snapshot-evaluation context MAY call functions that themselves call functions or deterministic external functions with out or inout parameters, because restriction j) does not apply recursively.
requirements.original: NOTE 7: The restriction of calling functions and deterministic external functions with out or inout parameters does not apply recursively, i.e. calling functions that themselves call functions with out or inout parameters is legal.

requirements.subject: ent:error
requirements.canonical: Using out or inout parameters or the `setencode` operation in a function called from a snapshot-evaluation context IS an error, because it may lead to different results of subsequent evaluations of the same snapshot.
requirements.original: NOTE 8: Using out or inout parameters and the setencode operation causes an error because this may lead to different results of subsequent evaluations of the same snapshot.

requirements.subject: ent:error
requirements.canonical: Calling functions and external functions with `@fuzzy` parameters from a snapshot-evaluation context IS an error, because fuzzy objects are re-evaluated each time they are referenced, which may lead to different results of subsequent evaluations of the same snapshot.
requirements.original: NOTE 9: Calling functions and external functions with @fuzzy parameters causes an error, because fuzzy objects are re-evaluated each time referenced and this may lead to different results of subsequent evaluations of the same snapshot.

requirements.subject: ent:module-control-function
requirements.canonical: An explicit control function IS declared either by use of the name `control` or by use of the `@control` modifier.
requirements.original: Explicit control functions are declared either by use of the name control or by use of the @control modifier.

requirements.subject: ent:module-control-function
requirements.canonical: An explicit control function SHALL NOT declare a `system` clause.
requirements.original: a) No system and no mtc clause shall be declared.

requirements.subject: ent:module-control-function
requirements.canonical: An explicit control function SHALL NOT declare an `mtc` clause.
requirements.original: a) No system and no mtc clause shall be declared.

requirements.subject: ent:component-type
requirements.canonical: The component type referenced in the `runs on` clause of an explicit control function SHALL NOT contain any port definitions.
requirements.original: b) The component type referenced in the runs on clause shall not contain any port definitions.

requirements.subject: ent:formal-parameter
requirements.canonical: A formal parameter and the return type of an explicit control function SHALL NOT be of a port type.
requirements.original: c) Parameters and the return type shall not be of a port type and shall not be of a structured type that contains fields of a port type on any level of nesting.

requirements.subject: ent:formal-parameter
requirements.canonical: A formal parameter and the return type of an explicit control function SHALL NOT be of a structured type that contains fields of a port type on any level of nesting.
requirements.original: c) Parameters and the return type shall not be of a port type and shall not be of a structured type that contains fields of a port type on any level of nesting.

requirements.subject: ent:formal-parameter
requirements.canonical: A formal parameter and the return type of a module control function SHALL NOT be of a default type.
requirements.original: d) Parameters and the return type of module control functions shall not be of a default type and shall not be of a structured type that contains fields of a default type on any level of nesting.

requirements.subject: ent:formal-parameter
requirements.canonical: A formal parameter and the return type of a module control function SHALL NOT be of a structured type that contains fields of a default type on any level of nesting.
requirements.original: d) Parameters and the return type of module control functions shall not be of a default type and shall not be of a structured type that contains fields of a default type on any level of nesting.

requirements.subject: ent:module-control-function
requirements.canonical: A statement or operation used in an explicit control function SHALL follow the usability restrictions for control functions given in the referenced table.
requirements.original: e) The restrictions on the use of statements and operations usable in control functions given in table 15 shall be followed.

ambiguity.issue: The sentence refers to "table 15", but table 15 is the list of predefined functions (clause 16.1.2); the overview of statements and operations and their usability is table 16 (clause 18). Chose the reading that the statement/operation overview is meant.
readings: A statement or operation used in an explicit control function SHALL be one that table 16 (clause 18) marks as usable in control functions.
A predefined function called in an explicit control function SHALL be one that table 15 (clause 16.1.2) allows in control functions.

requirements.subject: ent:module-control-function
requirements.canonical: A module control function used as an execution entry point SHALL have public visibility.
requirements.original: f) Module control functions used as an execution entry point shall have public visibility.

requirements.subject: ent:module-control-function
requirements.condition: the module control function is invoked explicitly
requirements.canonical: When a module control function is invoked explicitly, the component type of its `runs on` clause SHALL be compatible with the test component type of the invoking control component.
requirements.original: g) When invoking a module control function explicitly, the compatibility to the test component type of the invoking control component as described in clause 6.3.2.7 need to be fulfilled.

requirements.subject: ent:not-implemented-function
requirements.canonical: The not-implemented function has the syntax `???` ["(" Expression ")"] [`return any`].
requirements.original: ??? ["(" Expression ")"] [return any]

requirements.subject: ent:not-implemented-function
requirements.canonical: The not-implemented function `???` IS a temporary place-holder for TTCN-3 source code that remains to be implemented.
requirements.original: The not-implemented function ??? is a temporary place-holder for TTCN-3 source code that remains to be implemented.

requirements.subject: ent:not-implemented-function
requirements.canonical: The not-implemented function `???` MAY be used as a value in any expression.
requirements.original: It can be used as value in any expression or as stand-alone statement (direct use).

requirements.subject: ent:not-implemented-function
requirements.canonical: The not-implemented function `???` MAY be used as a stand-alone statement.
requirements.original: It can be used as value in any expression or as stand-alone statement (direct use).

requirements.subject: ent:not-implemented-function
requirements.canonical: An invocation of the not-implemented function `???` MAY have an optional parameter that provides contextual information.
requirements.original: The optional parameter can be used to provide contextual information.

requirements.subject: ent:not-implemented-function
requirements.canonical: The parameter of the not-implemented function `???` SHALL be of the universal charstring type.
requirements.original: The parameter shall be of the universal charstring type.

requirements.subject: ent:ttcn3-tool
requirements.condition: the not-implemented function is invoked
requirements.canonical: When `???` is invoked, the test environment MAY provide an actual implementation and continue execution.
requirements.original: When ??? is invoked the test environment may provide an actual implementation and continue execution.

requirements.subject: ent:ttcn3-tool
requirements.condition: the not-implemented function is invoked
requirements.canonical: When `???` is invoked, the test environment MAY prompt the user to enter a required expression.
requirements.original: For example the user may be prompted to enter a required expression.

requirements.subject: ent:ttcn3-tool
requirements.canonical: An implementation submitted by the test environment for a `???` invocation IS NOT changed during test execution.
requirements.original: The submitted implementation does not change during test execution (similar to module parameters).

ambiguity.issue: "During test execution" and the comparison with module parameters do not say whether the implementation is fixed per test case execution or for the whole test run, nor whether it is fixed per `???` occurrence in the source code or per invocation.
readings: An implementation submitted for a `???` occurrence IS NOT changed for the remainder of the whole test run (like a module parameter value).
An implementation submitted for a `???` invocation IS NOT changed until the current test case execution ends.

requirements.subject: ent:not-implemented-function
requirements.condition: the test environment cannot provide an actual implementation
requirements.canonical: If the test environment cannot provide an actual implementation, an invocation of `???` SHALL cause a runtime error indicating not yet implemented code.
requirements.original: If the test environment cannot provide an actual implementation, an invocation of ??? shall cause a runtime error to indicate not yet implemented code.

requirements.subject: ent:not-implemented-function
requirements.canonical: The not-implemented function `???` IS intended as a helper for prototyping and interactive test development.
requirements.original: This function is intended as helper for prototyping and interactive test development.

requirements.subject: ent:ttcn3-tool
requirements.canonical: A TTCN-3 tool SHOULD provide an option to warn about usage of `???` in production code.
requirements.original: It is therefore recommended that TTCN-3 tools provide an option to warn about ??? usage in production code.

requirements.subject: ent:altstep
requirements.canonical: An altstep IS used to specify default behaviour or to structure the alternatives of an `alt` statement.
requirements.original: TTCN-3 uses altsteps to specify default behaviour or to structure the alternatives of an alt statement.

requirements.subject: ent:altstep
requirements.canonical: An altstep definition has the syntax `altstep` [`@control`] [`interleave`] AltstepIdentifier "(" [{(FormalValuePar | FormalTemplatePar) [","]}] ")" [`runs on` ComponentType] [`mtc` ComponentType] [`system` ComponentType] "{" {(VarInstance | TimerInstance | ConstDef | TemplateDef) [";"]} AltGuardList "}".
requirements.original:
altstep [ @control ] [ interleave ] AltstepIdentifier
  "(" [ { ( FormalValuePar | FormalTemplatePar ) [","] } ] ")"
  [ runs on ComponentType ] 
  [ mtc ComponentType ]
  [ system ComponentType ]
  "{" 
     { ( VarInstance | TimerInstance | ConstDef | TemplateDef ) [";"] }
     AltGuardList
  "}"

ambiguity.issue: The syntax block admits only FormalValuePar and FormalTemplatePar in the altstep formal parameter list, whereas restriction c) (16.2.0-s026) speaks of ports and timers passed in as parameters and clause 5.4 allows port and timer parameters for altsteps.
readings: An altstep formal parameter list SHALL contain only formal value parameters and formal template parameters.
An altstep formal parameter list MAY additionally contain formal port and timer parameters as defined in clause 5.4; the syntax block is incomplete.

requirements.subject: ent:altstep
requirements.canonical: An altstep IS a scope unit similar to a function.
requirements.original: Altsteps are scope units similar to functions.

requirements.subject: ent:altstep-body
requirements.canonical: An altstep body IS composed of an optional set of local definitions and a set of alternatives.
requirements.original: The altstep body defines an optional set of local definitions and a set of alternatives, the so-called top alternatives, that form the altstep body.

requirements.subject: ent:top-alternative
requirements.canonical: An alternative of an altstep body IS called a top alternative.
requirements.original: The altstep body defines an optional set of local definitions and a set of alternatives, the so-called top alternatives, that form the altstep body.

requirements.subject: ent:top-alternative
requirements.canonical: The syntax rules of the top alternatives of an altstep ARE identical to the syntax rules of the alternatives of an `alt` statement.
requirements.original: The syntax rules of the top alternatives are identical to the syntax rules of the alternatives of alt statements.

requirements.subject: ent:altstep
requirements.canonical: An altstep MAY define a named interleave statement by usage of the `interleave` keyword.
requirements.original: An altstep can also be used to define a named interleave statement by usage of the interleave keyword.

requirements.subject: ent:top-alternative
requirements.condition: the altstep is an interleave altstep
requirements.canonical: If an altstep is defined with the `interleave` keyword, the syntax rules of its top alternatives ARE identical to the syntax rules of the alternatives of an `interleave` statement.
requirements.original: In this case, the syntax rules of the top alternatives are identical to the syntax rules of the alternatives of the interleave statements.

requirements.subject: ent:interleave-altstep
requirements.canonical: The usage of an interleave altstep IS NOT subject to further restrictions than the usage of a normal altstep, because an interleave statement is semantically equivalent to the expanded alt statement.
requirements.original: NOTE: As an interleave statement is semantically equivalent with the expanded alt statement, there are no further restrictions on usages of interleave altsteps than on usages of normal altsteps.

requirements.subject: ent:interleave-altstep
requirements.canonical: An interleave altstep and a normal altstep CAN both be used as activated default alternatives and as top-level alternatives in other `alt` statement blocks.
requirements.original: They can both be used as activated default alternatives and as top-level alternatives in other alt statement blocks.

requirements.subject: ent:altstep
requirements.canonical: The behaviour of an altstep CAN be defined by using the program statements and operations summarized in clause 18.
requirements.original: The behaviour of an altstep can be defined by using the program statements and operations summarized in clause 18.

requirements.subject: ent:altstep
requirements.canonical: An altstep CAN invoke functions and altsteps.
requirements.original: Altsteps may invoke functions and altsteps or activate altsteps as defaults.

requirements.subject: ent:altstep
requirements.canonical: An altstep CAN activate altsteps as defaults.
requirements.original: Altsteps may invoke functions and altsteps or activate altsteps as defaults.

requirements.subject: ent:altstep
requirements.canonical: An altstep MAY be parameterized as defined in clause 5.4.
requirements.original: Altsteps may be parameterized as defined in clause 5.4.

requirements.subject: ent:altstep
requirements.canonical: An altstep MAY have an `mtc` clause.
requirements.original: Altsteps may have an mtc clause.

requirements.subject: ent:mtc-clause
requirements.condition: the altstep has an mtc clause
requirements.canonical: If an altstep has an `mtc` clause, the component type referenced by the `mtc` clause SHALL be mtc-compatible with the type of the mtc component reference.
requirements.original: If an altstep has an mtc clause, the type referenced by this clause shall be mtccompatible (see clause 6.3.2.7) with the type of the mtc component reference.

requirements.subject: ent:component-reference
requirements.condition: the altstep has no mtc clause
requirements.canonical: If an altstep has no `mtc` clause, the type of the mtc component reference IS unknown in the scope of the altstep.
requirements.original: If the mtc clause is not present, the type of the mtc component reference is unknown in the scope of this altstep.

requirements.subject: ent:altstep
requirements.canonical: An altstep MAY have a `system` clause.
requirements.original: Altsteps may have a system clause.

requirements.subject: ent:system-clause
requirements.condition: the altstep has a system clause
requirements.canonical: If an altstep has a `system` clause, the component type referenced by the `system` clause SHALL be system-compatible with the type of the system component reference.
requirements.original: If an altstep has a system clause, the type referenced by this clause shall by system-compatible (see clause 6.3.2.7) with the type of the system component reference.

requirements.subject: ent:component-reference
requirements.condition: the altstep has no system clause
requirements.canonical: If an altstep has no `system` clause, the type of the system component reference IS unknown in the scope of the altstep.
requirements.original: If the system clause is not present, the type of the system component reference is unknown in the scope of this altstep.

requirements.subject: ent:altstep
requirements.condition: the altstep has the @control modifier
requirements.canonical: An altstep with the `@control` modifier SHALL be executed only on the control component.
requirements.original: Altsteps with the @control modifier are allowed to be executed only on the control component (see clause 26).

requirements.subject: ent:altstep
requirements.condition: the altstep has the @control modifier
requirements.canonical: An altstep with the `@control` modifier SHALL fulfil the restrictions specified for functions with the `@control` modifier.
requirements.original: The restrictions specified for functions with the @control modifier (see clause 16.1.5) are valid for these altsteps as well.

requirements.subject: ent:local-definition
requirements.canonical: A local definition of an altstep SHALL be defined before the set of top alternatives.
requirements.original: a) The local definitions of an altstep shall be defined before the set of alternatives.

requirements.subject: ent:default-value
requirements.canonical: The evaluation of default values of formal parameters and the initialization of local definitions of an altstep by calling value returning functions CAN have side effects.
requirements.original: b) The evaluation of formal parameters' default values and initialization of local definitions by calling value returning functions may have side effects.

requirements.subject: ent:default-value
requirements.canonical: The default value of a formal parameter of an altstep SHALL fulfil the restrictions given in clause 16.1.4.
requirements.original: To avoid side effects that cause an inconsistency between the actual snapshot and the state of the component, and to prevent different results of subsequent evaluations on an unchanged snapshot, restrictions given in clause 16.1.4 shall apply to the formal parameters' default values and the initialization of local definitions.

requirements.subject: ent:local-definition
requirements.canonical: The initialization of a local definition of an altstep SHALL fulfil the restrictions given in clause 16.1.4.
requirements.original: To avoid side effects that cause an inconsistency between the actual snapshot and the state of the component, and to prevent different results of subsequent evaluations on an unchanged snapshot, restrictions given in clause 16.1.4 shall apply to the formal parameters' default values and the initialization of local definitions.

requirements.subject: ent:altstep
requirements.condition: the altstep includes port operations or uses component variables, constants or timers
requirements.canonical: If an altstep includes port operations or uses component variables, component constants or component timers, the altstep header SHALL reference the associated component type by a `runs on` clause.
requirements.original: c) If an altstep includes port operations or uses component variables, constants or timers the associated component type shall be referenced using the `runs on` keywords in the altstep header.

requirements.subject: ent:altstep
requirements.condition: all ports, variables, constants and timers used within the altstep are passed in as parameters
requirements.canonical: If all ports, variables, constants and timers used within an altstep are passed in as parameters, the altstep MAY omit the `runs on` clause.
requirements.original: The one exception to this rule is if all ports, variables, constants and timers used within the altstep are passed in as parameters.

requirements.subject: ent:altstep
requirements.condition: the altstep has no runs on clause
requirements.canonical: An altstep without a `runs on` clause SHALL NOT locally invoke a function or altstep with a `runs on` clause.
requirements.original: d) An altstep without a `runs on` clause shall never invoke a function or altstep or activate an altstep as default with a `runs on` clause locally.

requirements.subject: ent:altstep
requirements.condition: the altstep has no runs on clause
requirements.canonical: An altstep without a `runs on` clause SHALL NOT locally activate an altstep with a `runs on` clause as default.
requirements.original: d) An altstep without a `runs on` clause shall never invoke a function or altstep or activate an altstep as default with a `runs on` clause locally.

requirements.subject: ent:altstep
requirements.condition: the altstep is activated as a default
requirements.canonical: An altstep that is activated as a default SHALL only have `in` value or `in` template parameters.
requirements.original: e) An altstep that is activated as a default shall only have `in` value or template parameters.

requirements.subject: ent:altstep
requirements.condition: the altstep is never activated as a default
requirements.canonical: An altstep that is only invoked as an alternative in an `alt` statement or as a stand-alone statement MAY have `in`, `out` and `inout` parameters.
requirements.original: An altstep that is only invoked as an alternative in an `alt` statement or as stand-alone statement in a TTCN-3 behaviour description may have `in`, `out` and `inout` parameters.

requirements.subject: ent:formal-parameter-list
requirements.canonical: The formal parameter list of an altstep SHALL follow the rules for formal parameter lists defined in clause 5.4.
requirements.original: The rules for formal parameter lists shall be followed as defined in clause 5.4.

requirements.subject: ent:altstep
requirements.condition: the altstep is started by the start test component operation
requirements.canonical: An altstep started by the start test component operation SHALL have a `runs on` clause.
requirements.original: f) Altsteps started by using the start test component operation shall always have a runs on clause (see clause 22.5) and are considered to be invoked in the component to be started, i.e. not locally.

requirements.subject: ent:altstep
requirements.condition: the altstep is started by the start test component operation
requirements.canonical: An altstep started by the start test component operation IS considered to be invoked in the component to be started, not locally.
requirements.original: f) Altsteps started by using the start test component operation shall always have a runs on clause (see clause 22.5) and are considered to be invoked in the component to be started, i.e. not locally.

requirements.subject: ent:start-component-operation
requirements.canonical: The start test component operation MAY be invoked within behaviour without a `runs on` clause.
requirements.original: However, the start test component operation may be invoked within behaviour without a runs on clause.

requirements.subject: ent:top-alternative
requirements.condition: the altstep is an interleave altstep
requirements.canonical: If an altstep is an interleave altstep, all restrictions of the `interleave` statement SHALL apply to the top alternatives of the altstep.
requirements.original: g) If the altstep is an interleave altstep, all restrictions of the interleave statement (see clause 20.4) apply to the top alternatives of the altstep as well.

requirements.subject: ent:altstep-invocation
requirements.canonical: An altstep invocation IS always related to an `alt` statement.
requirements.original: The invocation of an altstep is always related to an alt statement.

requirements.subject: ent:altstep-invocation
requirements.canonical: An altstep CAN be invoked either implicitly by the default mechanism or explicitly by a direct call within an `alt` statement.
requirements.original: The invocation may be done either implicitly by the default mechanism (see clause C.5) or explicitly by a direct call within an alt statement (see clause 20.2).

requirements.subject: ent:altstep-invocation
requirements.canonical: An altstep invocation has the syntax [`@nodefault`] AltstepRef "(" [{ActualPar [","]}] ")".
requirements.original: [ @nodefault ] AltstepRef "(" [ { ActualPar [","] } ] ")"

requirements.subject: ent:altstep-invocation
requirements.canonical: An altstep invocation IS NOT causing a new snapshot to be taken.
requirements.original: The invocation of an altstep causes no new snapshot and the evaluation of the top alternatives of an altstep is done by using the actual snapshot of the alt statement from which the altstep was called.

requirements.subject: ent:top-alternative
requirements.canonical: The top alternatives of an invoked altstep ARE evaluated by using the actual snapshot of the `alt` statement from which the altstep was called.
requirements.original: The invocation of an altstep causes no new snapshot and the evaluation of the top alternatives of an altstep is done by using the actual snapshot of the alt statement from which the altstep was called.

requirements.subject: ent:snapshot
requirements.condition: a new alt statement is entered within a selected top alternative
requirements.canonical: If a new `alt` statement is specified and entered within a selected top alternative of an altstep, a new snapshot IS taken.
requirements.original: NOTE 1: A new snapshot within an altstep will of course be taken, if within a selected top alternative a new alt statement is specified and entered.

requirements.subject: ent:altstep
requirements.condition: the altstep is invoked implicitly by the default mechanism
requirements.canonical: For an implicit invocation by means of the default mechanism, an altstep SHALL be activated as a default by an `activate` statement before the place of the invocation is reached.
requirements.original: For an implicit invocation of an altstep by means of the default mechanism, the altstep shall be activated as a default by means of an activate statement before the place of the invocation is reached.

requirements.subject: ent:altstep-invocation
requirements.canonical: An explicit call of an altstep within an `alt` statement IS written like a function invocation as an alternative.
requirements.original: An explicit call of an altstep within an alt statement looks syntactically like a function invocation as an alternative.

requirements.subject: ent:altstep-invocation
requirements.condition: the altstep is called explicitly within an alt statement
requirements.canonical: When an altstep is called explicitly within an `alt` statement, the next alternative to be checked IS the first top alternative of the altstep.
requirements.original: When an altstep is called explicitly within an alt statement, the next alternative to be checked is the first alternative of the altstep.

requirements.subject: ent:top-alternative
requirements.canonical: The top alternatives of an explicitly called altstep ARE checked and executed in the same way as the alternatives of an `alt` statement, except that no new snapshot is taken when entering the altstep.
requirements.original: The alternatives of the altstep are checked and executed the same way as alternatives of an alt statement (see clause 20.1) with the exception that no new snapshot is taken when entering the altstep.

requirements.subject: ent:altstep-invocation
requirements.condition: unsuccessful termination of the altstep and the call is not the last alternative
requirements.canonical: If all top alternatives of an explicitly called altstep have been checked without a matching branch and the call is not the last alternative of the `alt` statement, the next alternative of the `alt` statement IS evaluated.
requirements.original: An unsuccessful termination of the altstep (i.e. all top alternatives of the altstep have been checked and no matching branch is found) causes the evaluation of the next alternative or invocation of the default mechanism (if the explicit call is the last alternative of the alt statement).

requirements.subject: ent:altstep-invocation
requirements.condition: unsuccessful termination of the altstep and the call is the last alternative
requirements.canonical: If all top alternatives of an explicitly called altstep have been checked without a matching branch and the call is the last alternative of the `alt` statement, the default mechanism IS invoked.
requirements.original: An unsuccessful termination of the altstep (i.e. all top alternatives of the altstep have been checked and no matching branch is found) causes the evaluation of the next alternative or invocation of the default mechanism (if the explicit call is the last alternative of the alt statement).

requirements.subject: ent:altstep-invocation
requirements.condition: the altstep ends with a stop statement
requirements.canonical: If the selected top alternative of an explicitly called altstep ends with a `stop` statement, the test component IS terminated.
requirements.original: A successful termination may cause either the termination of the test component, i.e. the altstep ends with a stop statement, or a new snapshot and re-evaluation of the alt statement, i.e. the altstep ends with repeat (see clause 20.2) or a continuation immediately after the alt statement, i.e. the execution of the selected top alternative of the altstep ends with a break statement (see clause 19.12) or without explicit repeat or stop.

requirements.subject: ent:altstep-invocation
requirements.condition: the altstep ends with repeat
requirements.canonical: If the selected top alternative of an explicitly called altstep ends with a `repeat` statement, a new snapshot IS taken and the calling `alt` statement IS re-evaluated.
requirements.original: A successful termination may cause either the termination of the test component, i.e. the altstep ends with a stop statement, or a new snapshot and re-evaluation of the alt statement, i.e. the altstep ends with repeat (see clause 20.2) or a continuation immediately after the alt statement, i.e. the execution of the selected top alternative of the altstep ends with a break statement (see clause 19.12) or without explicit repeat or stop.

requirements.subject: ent:altstep-invocation
requirements.condition: the selected top alternative ends with break or without explicit repeat or stop
requirements.canonical: If the selected top alternative of an explicitly called altstep ends with a `break` statement or without an explicit `repeat` or `stop`, execution IS continued immediately after the calling `alt` statement.
requirements.original: A successful termination may cause either the termination of the test component, i.e. the altstep ends with a stop statement, or a new snapshot and re-evaluation of the alt statement, i.e. the altstep ends with repeat (see clause 20.2) or a continuation immediately after the alt statement, i.e. the execution of the selected top alternative of the altstep ends with a break statement (see clause 19.12) or without explicit repeat or stop.

requirements.subject: ent:top-alternative
requirements.canonical: An alternative in an explicitly invoked altstep CAN refer to a disconnected or unmapped port at the time of its evaluation.
requirements.original: NOTE 2: Due to the possibility of defining dynamic test configurations, an alternative in an explicitly invoked altstep may refer to a disconnected or unmapped port at the time of its evaluation.

requirements.subject: ent:port
requirements.canonical: A port IS owned by the receiving component.
requirements.original: In TTCN-3, ports belong to the receiving component and matching is related to the top elements in the port queues.

requirements.subject: ent:port-queue
requirements.canonical: Matching IS related to the top elements in the port queues.
requirements.original: In TTCN-3, ports belong to the receiving component and matching is related to the top elements in the port queues.

requirements.subject: ent:port
requirements.canonical: A dynamically unmapped or disconnected port contributes to a snapshot in the same manner as a mapped or connected port.
requirements.original: Dynamically unmapped and disconnected ports contribute to a snapshot in the same manner as mapped and connected ports.

requirements.subject: ent:altstep
requirements.canonical: An explicitly invoked altstep CAN execute receiving operations that empty the queues of unmapped and disconnected ports without causing a test case error.
requirements.original: This means, an explicitly invoked altstep may execute receiving operations that empty the queues of unmapped and disconnected ports without causing a test case error.

requirements.subject: ent:altstep
requirements.canonical: An altstep MAY be called as a stand-alone statement in a TTCN-3 behaviour description.
requirements.original: An altstep can also be called as a stand-alone statement in a TTCN-3 behaviour description.

requirements.subject: ent:altstep-invocation
requirements.canonical: A stand-alone call of an altstep IS a shorthand for an `alt` statement with only one alternative describing the explicit call of the altstep.
requirements.original: In this case, the call of the altstep can be interpreted as shorthand for an alt statement with only one alternative describing the explicit call of the altstep.

requirements.subject: ent:nodefault-modifier
requirements.condition: the @nodefault modifier is placed before a stand-alone altstep call
requirements.canonical: If the `@nodefault` modifier is placed before a stand-alone altstep call, the implicit `alt` statement IS also modified by `@nodefault`.
requirements.original: If the @nodefault modifier is placed before a stand-alone altstep call, the implicit alt statement also contains the @nodefault modifier.

requirements.subject: ent:altstep-invocation
requirements.canonical: When an altstep is invoked, the test component type of the invoking test component SHALL be compatible with the component type of the altstep `runs on` clause.
requirements.original: a) When invoking an altstep, the compatibility of the test component type of the invoking test component and of the altstep runs on clause (as described in clause 6.3.2.7) need to be fulfilled.

requirements.subject: ent:altstep-invocation
requirements.canonical: When an altstep is invoked, the component type of the `mtc` clause of the invoked altstep SHALL be mtc-compatible with the actual mtc type of the running test case.
requirements.original: c) When invoking an altstep, the mtc and system compatibility of the mtc and system components of the invoked altstep with the actual mtc and system types of the running test case as described in clause 6.3.2.7 need to be fulfilled.

requirements.subject: ent:altstep-invocation
requirements.canonical: When an altstep is invoked, the component type of the `system` clause of the invoked altstep SHALL be system-compatible with the actual system type of the running test case.
requirements.original: c) When invoking an altstep, the mtc and system compatibility of the mtc and system components of the invoked altstep with the actual mtc and system types of the running test case as described in clause 6.3.2.7 need to be fulfilled.

requirements.subject: ent:testcase
requirements.canonical: A test case IS a complete and independent specification of the actions required to achieve a specific test purpose.
requirements.original: A test case is complete and independent specification of the actions required to achieve a specific test purpose.

requirements.subject: ent:testcase
requirements.canonical: A test case typically starts in a stable testing state and ends in a stable testing state.
requirements.original: It typically starts in a stable testing state and ends in a stable testing state.

requirements.subject: ent:testcase
requirements.canonical: A test case CAN involve one or more consecutive or concurrent connections to the SUT.
requirements.original: It may involve one or more consecutive or concurrent connections to the SUT.

requirements.subject: ent:testcase
requirements.canonical: A test case SHALL be complete in the sense that it is sufficient to enable a test verdict to be assigned unambiguously to each potentially observable test outcome.
requirements.original: The test case shall be complete in the sense that it is sufficient to enable a test verdict to be assigned unambiguously to each potentially observable test outcome (i.e. sequence of test events).

requirements.subject: ent:testcase
requirements.canonical: A test case SHALL be independent in the sense that the derived executable test case can be executed in isolation from other test cases.
requirements.original: The test case shall be independent in the sense that it shall be possible to execute the derived executable test case in isolation from other such test cases.

requirements.subject: ent:testcase
requirements.canonical: A test case IS a special kind of function.
requirements.original: In TTCN-3, test cases are a special kind of function.

requirements.subject: ent:testcase
requirements.canonical: A test case defines the behaviour that is executed to check whether the SUT passes a test or not.
requirements.original: Test cases define the behaviour, which have to be executed to check whether the SUT passes a test or not.

requirements.subject: ent:mtc
requirements.canonical: The behaviour of a test case IS performed by the MTC.
requirements.original: This behaviour is performed by the MTC which is automatically created when a test case is being executed.

requirements.subject: ent:mtc
requirements.canonical: The MTC IS created automatically when a test case is executed.
requirements.original: This behaviour is performed by the MTC which is automatically created when a test case is being executed.

requirements.subject: ent:testcase
requirements.canonical: A test case definition has the syntax `testcase` TestcaseIdentifier "(" [{(FormalValuePar | FormalTemplatePar) [","]}] ")" [`runs on` ComponentType] [`system` ComponentType] StatementBlock.
requirements.original:
testcase TestcaseIdentifier
  "(" [ { ( FormalValuePar | FormalTemplatePar) [","] } ] ")"
  [ runs on ComponentType ]
  [ system ComponentType ] 
  StatementBlock

requirements.subject: ent:verdict
requirements.canonical: The result of a test case execution IS a test verdict.
requirements.original: The result of a test case execution is a test verdict.

requirements.subject: ent:testcase-header
requirements.canonical: A test case header IS composed of two parts: an interface part and a test system part.
requirements.original: A test case header has two parts:

requirements.subject: ent:testcase-header
requirements.canonical: The interface part of a test case header IS optional and IS denoted by the keywords `runs on`, which reference the required component type for the MTC.
requirements.original: a) interface part (optional): denoted by the keyword runs `on which references the required component type for` the MTC and makes the associated port names visible within the MTC behaviour.

requirements.subject: ent:port
requirements.canonical: The port names of the component type referenced by the `runs on` clause of a test case ARE visible within the MTC behaviour.
requirements.original: a) interface part (optional): denoted by the keyword runs `on which references the required component type for` the MTC and makes the associated port names visible within the MTC behaviour.

requirements.subject: ent:mtc
requirements.condition: the runs on clause is missing
requirements.canonical: If the `runs on` clause of a test case is missing, the MTC created by the test case has no ports, no component constants and no component variables.
requirements.original: In case the runs `on clause` is missing, the MTC created by the test case has no ports, and no component constants and variables;

requirements.subject: ent:testcase-header
requirements.canonical: The test system part of a test case header IS optional and IS denoted by the keyword `system`, which references the component type that defines the required ports for the test system interface.
requirements.original: b) test system part (optional): denoted by the keyword system which references the component type which defines the required ports for the test system interface.

requirements.subject: ent:system-clause
requirements.condition: the test case has no system clause
requirements.canonical: The `system` clause of a test case SHALL only be omitted if only the MTC is instantiated during test execution.
requirements.original: The test system part shall only be omitted if, during test execution, only the MTC is instantiated.

ambiguity.issue: The sentence does not say whether a violation is a compile-time error or a runtime error, i.e. whether tools have to detect statically that a test case without system clause creates PTCs.
readings: A test case without a `system` clause that contains a `create` operation for a PTC SHALL be rejected at compile time.
Creating a PTC during the execution of a test case without a `system` clause SHALL cause a runtime error.

requirements.subject: ent:test-system-interface
requirements.condition: the system clause is omitted and the runs on clause is present
requirements.canonical: If the `system` clause of a test case is omitted and the `runs on` clause is present, the MTC type implicitly defines the test system interface ports.
requirements.original: In this case, the MTC type defines the test system interface ports implicitly if the runs `on clause is present.

requirements.subject: ent:test-system-interface
requirements.condition: both runs on and system clauses are missing
requirements.canonical: If both the `runs on` and the `system` clause of a test case are missing, the test system interface IS without ports.
requirements.original: If both runs` `on and system clauses are missing, the test system` interface has no ports;

requirements.subject: ent:formal-parameter
requirements.canonical: The type of every formal parameter of a test case SHALL be a data type.
requirements.original: c) all formal parameter types of the test case shall be of a data type.

requirements.subject: ent:testcase
requirements.canonical: The behaviour of a test case CAN be defined by using the program statements and operations described in clause 18.
requirements.original: The behaviour of a test case can be defined by using the program statements and operations described in clause 18.

requirements.subject: ent:testcase
requirements.canonical: A test case MAY be parameterized as described in clause 5.4.
requirements.original: Test cases may be parameterized as described in clause 5.4.

requirements.subject: ent:testcase
requirements.canonical: A test case MAY be executed from a control behaviour definition.
requirements.original: Test cases can be executed from control behaviour definitions (see clause 26).

requirements.subject: ent:formal-parameter-list
requirements.canonical: The formal parameter list of a test case SHALL follow the rules for formal parameter lists defined in clause 5.4.
requirements.original: a) The rules for formal parameter lists shall be followed as defined in clause 5.4.

requirements.subject: ent:testcase
requirements.canonical: A test case SHALL only be invoked with an `execute` statement in a function or altstep running on a control component.
requirements.original: b) Test cases may only be invoked with an execute statement in a function or altstep running on a control component as defined in clause 26.
